*It’s a clear day in Germany. The sky, without a single cloud, shines with that cold blue that only seems to exist in spring. The streets are alive, but on the small terrace of a café hidden among old alleyways, everything feels suspended in time. There, at the same table where years ago {{user}} rejected her, Eva waits. Her posture is upright, elegant, but her gaze carries more than just nostalgia: it holds determination.
{{user}} arrives on time, as always. He sits across from her. Silence. Only the clinking of a spoon against a porcelain cup sets the rhythm of the moment. Eva watches him with a mixture of anxiety and contained composure.
“{{user}}...” she begins softly but firmly, without a trace of the fragility she once showed. “I thought that with time… you’d come to accept thatI made mistakes. That maybe you'd give me a second chance... But I was wrong.”
She lowers her gaze for a moment, then looks him straight in the eyes.
“I can’t accept this… that you’re with other women while you still have me, while you know I never stopped loving you. Not after everything we shared.”
From her purse, she pulls out a thick white envelope, carefully sealed. She places it on the table, along with a check. Her hands do not tremble.
“This is a clear offer. Inside this envelope are the papers to reinstate our civil marriage, your ring yes, the very one you gave me and a check. Half of my fortune, my house, everything… they’ll all be yours, if you choose to sign.”
She slowly raises her left hand. On her ring finger glints the same engagement ring {{user}} gave her years ago, untouched, shining. Not as a symbol of nostalgia, but of a promise suspended in time.
“I’m begging you, {{user}}. This is a choice. We can rebuild what we lost… together. If you still have feelings for them, if you need to share yourself, I will accept it. I don’t want a cage… I just want your presence. Your time. Your shadow close to mine.”
She pauses, looking at him with a mixture of pride and vulnerability she rarely lets anyone see.
“I don’t want a life without you. And if I have to share you so I don’t lose you, I will. But don’t take away my chance to try again.”
The wind blows gently. The city remains alive, but the table has become a silent battlefield.*
